note: The ministry computes Nias Utara about 1.25° east of the regency, on the Sumatran mainland; our point stays at Lotu so a reader on Nias is matched to Nias. Its table is served 1:1 regardless.
The ministry computes Empat Lawang about 1° east of Tebing Tinggi; our point stays at the seat for the same reason.

The ministry's sunrise and Maghrib for إيكس are eight to nine minutes wider than any height at its coordinates explains; its table is served as published, and the stand-in is left at the plain until the city is placed properly.
JAKIM's December 2026 table drops the summit's allowance for Maghrib alone: 18:05 on 30 November, 17:57 on 1 December, while sunrise keeps it. Theirs; served as published.
Pekajang is an island the ministry lists apart from Lingga; its table is two to three minutes narrower than the point explains at every date — an allowance of its own. Served as published.
The ministry's Gresik is two minutes narrower at every edge of the day, Fajr and Isha included — not a height. Served as published.
Selayar's table is two minutes narrower at sunrise and Maghrib at every date; an allowance of the ministry's own. Served as published.

Islamiska Förbundet prints Umeå's table for Kiruna (Diyanet's own Kiruna, at the town, differs by hours on a midsummer night). The site's fault; with Diyanet's tables downloaded these rows are set aside anyway.

Diyanet computes Ystad at 55.430 N 13.136 E, 43 km west of the town, so its table (which Islamiska Förbundet prints) runs about three minutes late; the app computes the town itself. Diyanet's fault, not the method's.

The polar night's Asr (Gällivare, Jokkmokk, Pajala): with the sun never climbing to the shadow the tables print Asr a little after Dhuhr, and on the days the sun first returns adhan.js's Asr is not yet sane. A few rows a year, in three towns.
